b6_reason: Interhalogen compounds are more reactive than the parent halogen (except F2) because the A-X bond is weaker than the X-X bond, so both statements hold and R explains A.
b6_note: Option 1 follows the standard textbook rule that A-X bonds in interhalogens are weaker than X-X bonds; tabulated bond enthalpies (I-Cl about 208 kJ/mol vs I-I about 151 kJ/mol) actually run the other way, so R is arguable and option 3 is a defensible alternative. Also, 'ICI' and 'I-CI' in the stem are mis-rendered 'ICl' and 'I-Cl' (capital I for lowercase l), and I2 lost its subscript.
